geometry_edits.rationale: Orient the stepping along the long axis so the mass remains a single continuous ribbon-like body.
Lower the number of step events to avoid arbitrary tiering and preserve hierarchy.
Tighten the setback so the terracing reads as capacity-bearing rather than over-clipped.
Bind the carve to the verified frontage side to activate the street threshold.
Increase the void depth to produce a readable public court rather than a superficial notch.

graph_edits.rationale: Retain the long bar anchor but convert the generic setback into a more explicit terraced mass so the section reads as one continuous inhabited landform.
Reduce the repetition of stepbacks so the dominant gesture stays legible and the silhouette reads as a singular terraced body.
Tighten the steps to preserve continuity and avoid a too-tiered or fragmented profile.
Align the public threshold with the verified access side so the void actually addresses the street edge.
Widen the carve to make the access response legible as public ground rather than a small incision.
Extend the notch vertically to strengthen the court/entry seam and improve void publicness.

rationale: The candidate has a coherent dominant gesture in all four views: a long stepped bar placed within the parcel, so it passes basic mass legibility and containment. However, it behaves mostly as a compact terraced extrusion with only a shallow notch and little true public void, so the access edge is not yet convincingly activated despite the verified frontage line. The silhouette is readable but tends toward repetitive stepping rather than a capacity-bearing terrace section, and the section logic does not yet demonstrate a strong neighborhood ground threshold or courtyard/public sequence. It resonates most with the terraced/courtyard references, but it remains closer to an organized box than to the more spatially operative neighborhood precedents. Because program_context requires an active ground edge and one clear public void or terrace, the form does not hard-pass program fit yet.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion/cultural than compact neighborhood-living; do not copy the roof curvature or scenic wall treatment.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise pavilion composition with a central void and an upper connector; good precedent for a readable public court and layered massing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than the candidate; tower/podium scale is not transferable here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like courtyard organization with stepped low-rise blocks around a shared open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more open and glazed; candidate is too sealed and too stepped to match directly.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise bar with a central void and sloping/folded roof logic supporting a public interior street.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is the strongest spatial precedent; candidate lacks the same carved public sequence and lightness.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced ribbon-like massing that responds to site slope with a legible promenade/courtyard sequence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate currently reads as a single tiered bar rather than interlocking volumes; avoid over-fragmentation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking low-rise volumes with a clear courtyard and void-under-block condition.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied, but public-threshold response to the verified access edge is weak.
The mass is coherent across views, so this is not a rejection for cross-view collision or incoherence.
The stepped section should become a more deliberate terrace/courtyard device rather than a generic tiered bar.
